messages:
maya: Quick FYI — started seeing p99 tail spikes on prod-serving around 10:15 UTC. Correlated with sustained concurrency ~350-420. KV cache eviction rate jumps in the same window.

sam: Can you paste the numbers? p95/p99?

maya: p95 ~120ms, p99 up to 820ms (tokens), baseline normally p99 ~230ms. KV metrics: evictions 380-420/s, live_entries dropping ~30% when spike happens.

jin: Do we have a flamegraph or callstack from the slow requests?

maya: attaching quick snippet from profiles (sampled):
```
# top stacks
serve_request -> perform_step -> kv_lookup -> lock_wait (45%)
kv_lookup -> cache_miss -> fetch_remote_kv (25%)
batch_coordinator -> microbatch_build (15%)
```

maya: Also saw many microbatch merges happening concurrently which increases KV working set for a short window.

alix: interesting — sounds like transient working set bursts cause evictions which then make later requests hit remote store. That explains tail.

sam: What are current batching heuristics? size / max_wait?

maya: config snippet from running hosts:
```
microbatch:
  max_batch_tokens: 4096
  max_batch_size: 32
  max_wait_ms: 10
kv_cache:
  max_entries_per_shard: 50k
  eviction_policy: lru_windowed
```

jin: With many concurrent requests each building a microbatch of ~32, peak combined KV entries spike. LRU windowed has a lag before evicting the right items. Under pressure you see many premature evictions then remote fetch latency bubbles into p99.

perf-bot: @channel perf-run: commit b3a7f9e — concurrency sweep (200/300/400) — results:
- microbatch=32: p95 115ms, p99 760ms @400
- microbatch=16: p95 130ms, p99 280ms @400
- microbatch=8:  p95 160ms, p99 240ms @400
(note: throughput drops ~18% at size=8)

maya: So smaller microbatches cut p99 significantly at cost of throughput. Latency SLOs are p95<150ms p99<400ms. size=16 gets us close for p99 but p95 regresses a bit.

sam: If we care about p99 under bursty concurrency maybe add two-tier policy: route latency-sensitive traffic to microbatch=8 path and throughput to 32. Can we do routing?

alix: Yes, we already have routing by route tags. But that halves effective capacity unless we autoscale. Another idea: change KV policy to decaying-LRU with larger protected window so hot keys survive bursts.

jin: I tried a sim locally: increasing max_entries_per_shard to 80k reduced evictions 3x, p99 improved to ~310ms at microbatch=32. But memory usage + GC pressure increased.

maya: Tradeoffs everywhere. Also noticed kernel selection effects — bigger batches trigger different attention kernels that are a tad slower per-token on short prompts, pushing p95.

sam: So three levers: microbatch sizing, KV sizing/policy, kernel selection threshold. We need a matrix of experiments.

perf-bot: queued experiments: matrix: microbatch {8,16,32} x kv_entries {50k,80k} x kernel_threshold {seq_len 128,256}. ETA ~3h.

alix: For immediate mitigation, propose a short-lived config: set microbatch default for public route to 16 and enable prefix_kv_caching for top 5% hot routes. That should tame evictions without large mem bump.

maya: I'll roll a canary of microbatch=16 + prefix caching to 5% of traffic for 30m. Will watch p95/p99 and evictions.

jin: Add a temp metric: 'kv_backpressure_count' to track when requests stall on kv lookup lock — want to see if lock_wait remains dominant.

ops-bot: deploy started: canary group=5% routeset=public-mt microbatch=16 prefix_kv=true — deploy_id=deploy-2026-03-17-0733

sam: :eyes: keep logs open. If p99 < 400 and evictions drop -> expand. If p95 regresses >200 -> rollback.

maya: Canary shows initial win: evictions down 65%, p99 ~290ms at 5% traffic. Expanding to 25% now.

perf-bot: interim report @1775003350: canary->25%: p95 135ms, p99 310ms, throughput ~-6%

maya: Good signal. I'll open a follow-up thread with full flamegraphs and heap profiles. For now marking this thread actionable. :thumbsup:

sam: Nice work — let's keep KV sizing and kernel threshold experiments running in parallel.

jin: I'll post the flamegraph link and the sim scripts in the eng-runtime docs after lunch.

maya: thanks all. closing loop once we have full rollout data.
